Haarklous online in Unreal Engine 5 – report

27 October 2026. The whole game is rebuilt in Unreal Engine 5.8 with assets made by Blender scripts. Every item in the porting checklist is built and ticked; the game logic is a line-by-line C++ port of the web game, checked against the web code's own answers; every feature was played through with a simulated DualShock 4; online play was tested together with the web game on the separate test server. What still needs you: a test with the real DualShock 4 and a real microphone.

How to start the game

  • From the project: "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.exe" unreal\Haarklous\Haarklous.uproject -game -dx11 (from C:\Users\Lenovo\Documents\haarklous-ue5). Add -fullscreen for full screen.
  • Packaged build: double-click dist\Haarklous-UE5\Windows\Haarklous.exe (Shipping build, 1.1 GB, made with powershell -File tools\package-game.ps1; checked by running the screenshot tour in it). dist is not in git; the script makes it again in a few minutes.
  • Plug in the DualShock 4 (USB or Bluetooth) before starting; keyboard and mouse always work.
  • Online is off. To try it, start with -HKOnline (it only knows the test server wss://haarklous-ue5-test.server-smoke.workers.dev). The live game is never contacted.

What was built

The checklist (docs/PORTING-CHECKLIST.md) names the Unreal class or asset for every item. In short:

  • Game logic in C++, ported 1:1 from the JavaScript (unreal/Haarklous/Source/Haarklous): player and collision (FHKWalkWorld), apartment, doors, drinks and the drunk effect, stairwells (AHKGame), motorcycle, cars, excavator, helicopter, plane and FPV drone (HKVehicles, HKAircraft), disc golf and petanque (HKMinigames), firepit (HKFire), hostage-rescue mission (HKMission), photo camera, gallery, watch, map, chat (HKGameExtras), sound and music (HKSynth: the web's Web Audio sounds rebuilt in C++), menus and HUD (HKGameHud), DualShock 4 by raw HID with the web's mapping plus keyboard and mouse (HKInput), online play (HKNet, HKMultiplayer, AHKOnline, voice through the web's own game-voice.js).
  • Same numbers as the web: all speeds, physics constants, rules, coordinates and the vehicle list (seed 1707) are taken from the JavaScript. Nothing about gameplay was changed.
  • New graphics (made by scripts, rebuildable): the web's geometry is exported from the web game in headless Chrome, rebuilt in Blender (tools/blender) and imported into Unreal (tools/unreal). New ground material (grass, asphalt, gravel and sand blended by the map), new 3D trees and bushes at the web's exact spots, a physical sky with the web's clouds, distant hills and the fjord, a sun with soft shadows, baked indirect light in the apartment, stairwells and streets, glowing lamps, fire with flames, sparks and smoke.
  • Laptop settings: no Lumen, Nanite, virtual shadow maps or ray tracing; baked lighting (Lightmass), cascaded sun shadows, DirectX 11, screen percentage 75 % (graphics quality "Balanced"; "Fast" uses 65 %, "Sharp" 100 %).

How it was tested

Each one starts the real game (tools\run-game.ps1 -Test <name>), presses buttons and moves sticks like a player, checks the game state and takes screenshots. The last full round (27 Oct 2026, after the final lighting bake) passed every check in every play-through.

Online, on the test server only

The cloud server was copied unchanged to server/ with only the Worker name changed to haarklous-ue5-test, tested with npx wrangler dev, then deployed to your Cloudflare account at haarklous-ue5-test.server-smoke.workers.dev. The live game haarklous-online was never touched or contacted. The real Unreal game and the web game served by the test Worker joined one lobby by its code and ran a scripted session twice in a row, both times with 0 failures:

  • Join by code: both in lobby G3M8 (and BNU7 in the other run).
  • Chat both ways.
  • Doors: the web opened a door and Unreal showed it open; Unreal opened one and the web showed it open.
  • Firepit: one log from each side; both sides show the same fire level.
  • See each other move: the web player walked 6.1 m and Unreal saw the avatar move at up to 1.57 m/s; Unreal walked and the web saw it.
  • Passenger, web drives: Unreal got "□ Ride along with Web tester (passenger)", took the seat, and rode 8.0 m with the camera in the seat.
  • Passenger, Unreal drives: the web player rode pillion on Unreal's motorcycle for 5.5 m (avatar exactly at the pillion seat on both sides).
  • Voice: Unreal's microphone (a 440 Hz test tone) was heard by the web game (RMS 0.21, about 434 Hz), and Unreal heard the web's microphone (RMS 0.07). Voice uses the web's own game-voice.js in a hidden browser inside the game, so it is the same WebRTC voice as the web version.

Frame rates on this laptop

Measured on 27 Oct 2026 with tools\run-game.ps1 -Test fps -Res 2240x1400 -Fullscreen: full screen at the laptop's own resolution (2240 × 1400), graphics quality "Balanced" (the default, 75 % screen percentage), baked lighting, nothing else running. At each place the camera turns one full circle in 12 seconds, so every direction counts.

PlaceAverageSlowest 1 % of framesSlowest single frame
Home (apartment, looking into the living room and out of the windows)38.9 fps24.4 fps15.1 fps
Firepit (fire, smoke, cars and the block behind)32.2 fps24.1 fps20.8 fps
The park (Torshovdalen, the most trees)32.3 fps24.9 fps21.7 fps
The street outside 17A32.1 fps23.4 fps20.2 fps
Flying (110 m above the district)35.6 fps27.0 fps21.9 fps

All places stay above the 20 fps goal on average and in the slowest 1 % of frames. The one slow frame at home (15 fps) is a single hitch while turning, not a steady rate. During the online test, with a second game (the web version in software-rendered Chrome) running on the same laptop, the Unreal game still averaged 19.6 fps. The "Fast" (65 %, no shadows) and "Sharp" (100 %) settings were not measured.

What still needs you

  • Test with your real DualShock 4 (USB and Bluetooth). The controller code reads the same raw reports the browser uses and is tested with recorded reports and a simulated pad, but not with the real controller.
  • Voice with a real microphone (tested with a test tone and Chrome's fake microphone). Windows may ask once for microphone access.
  • Decide on the web-game bugs in docs/GAMEPLAY-IDEAS.md (they are copied 1:1, as the rules say): petanque never ends after 13 points, petanque can freeze when no boule is left, and vehicle obstacles appear one update late. Fixing them is a small change in both games once you say yes.
  • Web pull request #4 (hidden stashes with boosts) was not in the snapshot; refresh the snapshot when it is merged.

Differences from the web that are only about looks

  • The ground uses real materials instead of the web's painted map; the web's "aerial imagery" option (online Esri photos) is not used.
  • Clouds come from the web's own sky formula but sit over a physical sky; the far hills and fjord are the web's shapes.
  • Lamp globes do not cast shadows, the apartment rooms get soft fill light (the web used a hemisphere light that shines through walls), and the stairwell lamps are lit on every landing (baked) instead of one lamp following you.
